result_text:
`analyzeLandscape` is now a second name for `updateLandscape`, with the same options and behaviour. The module compiles offline, but I did not run the CLI, so the help output and the report creation are checked by reading the code only.

What changed:

- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE` and its description ("…The landscape counterpart of the analysis commands; same as updateLandscape"), and listed it in the no-argument usage overview next to `updateLandscape`.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**: both names dispatch to the same `updateLandscape(args)` method. For `-help`, the usage now uses the name the user typed (`args[0]`), and picks the `analyzeLandscape` description when that name was typed. `updateLandscape -help` still prints its own description.
- **`README.md`**: there was no command list to update, so I added a short "Landscape report" section describing both names and an example `analyzeLandscape -analysisRoot <folder>` call.

I could not run `java -jar` to check `-help` output or confirm `_sokrates_landscape/` gets created, because the shell commands that launch Java needed approval I wasn't given. Those checks are still worth running before you rely on this.

I did not touch `CLAUDE.md`, which still lists only `updateLandscape` among the main commands. Nothing is committed.
